sources: catalog/r/releases.json (this project's own scrape of CRAN's stated min_os per macOS build, used verbatim for majors 4.0-4.6)

milestones.notes: install.packages()/the CRAN client has been part of base R since the first release
package namespaces (NAMESPACE) let a package hide internal functions from users and other packages
parallel package (merger of multicore + snow) added to the base distribution; process-based (fork/cluster), not threaded
first, experimental separate 64-bit Windows installer; merged into one combined 32/64-bit installer in 2.12.0; 32-bit dropped entirely in 4.2.0

atomic vectors/lists/expressions can hold more than 2^31-1 elements (up to 2^52) on 64-bit platforms; support in individual base functions (e.g. 1-D FFT, which()) was added gradually through later 3.x/4.x releases

download.file()/url() gain method="libcurl" for HTTPS on both Windows and Unix-alikes; libcurl becomes the Unix-alike default in 3.4.0. The actual TLS version negotiated depends on the system libcurl/OpenSSL R links against, not on the R version itself
JIT byte-code compiler enabled by default at level 3; all packages byte-compiled on installation by default from 3.5.0
data.frame()/read.table() stop converting character columns to factors by default
r"(...)" literal syntax, avoiding backslash-escaping in regexes and Windows paths
|> built into the parser; the _ placeholder for non-first-argument targets follows in 4.2.0
first native Apple Silicon (arm64) macOS build, alongside the continuing Intel build
UTF-8 becomes the native encoding on Windows via the switch to the Universal C Runtime (UCRT); requires Windows 10 1903+ for full effect. Same release drops 32-bit Windows builds

not from R/CRAN itself -- CRAN ships no Linux binaries at all, only source. Posit's r-builds packaging service provides prebuilt arm64 .deb/.rpm alongside amd64 for every R version it lists, which starts at 3.0.0

os_support.macos: none from CRAN; a separate, non-CRAN classic Mac OS / early Mac OS X port existed outside the official distribution
os_support.linux: none official; CRAN has never shipped Linux binaries -- build from source on any Unix-like system (some distros package R independently)

added: first stable release of R as an open-source, S-compatible statistical language and environment
limitations: no package namespaces -- all functions in an attached package are visible/callable (fixed 1.7)
no 64-bit Windows build (fixed 2.11, merged into one installer in 2.12)
no built-in parallel/multicore support -- concurrency needs a CRAN package like snow or multicore (merged into base as the parallel package in 2.14)
vectors/lists are capped at 2^31-1 elements (fixed by long vectors in 3.0)
no default byte-code JIT compilation of user functions (fixed 3.4; packages byte-compiled by default from 3.5)

data.frame()/read.table() convert character columns to factors by default (stringsAsFactors=TRUE); no raw string literals, so backslashes in regexes/Windows paths must be double-escaped (both fixed 4.0)
no native pipe operator or lambda shorthand -- piping requires the magrittr package's %>%, and anonymous functions must be written as function(x) ... (both added 4.1)
32-bit Windows builds still shipped, doubling the installer and toolchain surface to maintain (dropped 4.2)
no native async/await or coroutines; all concurrency is process-based (parallel package, or the third-party future/promises packages), never threaded within one R session
